cells.tense: Something in you is opening, and nothing has been poured in yet.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: This week, before you answer what you feel about something, give the pull one breath of room — you don't have to follow it anywhere.
cells.core:
What is at work in you is opening and orienting at once. You are ready to receive and pointed toward what is worth moving toward, and the fact that nothing specific has arrived yet is not a lack — it is the clean edge of the vessel. Being at a door and walking through it are different, and you can be entirely here without having arrived anywhere.
Stay at that edge. When something asks what you feel, pause a breath before answering — not to withhold, only so the pull can show itself before you name it. You may find it wants nothing from you yet. Practised that way, the pause starts showing you where the next genuine feeling comes from.
cells.sheetLine: You are open and pointed, and nothing has to be in the vessel yet.
cells.verb: opening to feeling before there's anything specific to feel for
cells.place: a room where you have already let the quiet in

cells.tense: By tomorrow this openness will already have been packed in with answers.
cells.act: bring the directed work to its full standing
cells.ask: Decide in advance how this should end and finish that verdict on a page — put the page away for a week and don't touch it again.
cells.core:
You know this openness is for something, so you are building across it before it has shown you what it is. You fill the quiet with the plan for where it will take you, the meaning it will carry, the person you will have become by then. That building keeps you from being shown anything — and it works, at a cost, because the answer you land on is yours and not the moment's.
Take one ending you already want and finish it somewhere it does not need you. Put the page away, leave it a week, and find out whether you were making room or sealing a door to keep the draft out. The page will tell you which.
cells.sheetLine: You are packing the openness in before it can show you anything.
cells.verb: opening to feeling before there's anything specific to feel for

cells.tense: Something in you was opening, and you still stand at a door already shut.
cells.act: complete what you began by beginning it
cells.ask: Find something you began and let fall quiet, and touch it for ten minutes as if new — no finish line, no accounting for the time gone.
cells.core:
The readiness is still in you, and it is aimed backwards, at the version of being open that already came and went before it became anything. You can feel the pull in memory; the present moment has not been let near enough to pull in its own right. That is a beginner's willingness facing a door already passed through.
More feeling will not bring it back. One fresh start will. Find some half-begun thing you let fall quiet, touch it for ten minutes with no goal this week, and let yourself be bad at it again. Beginning it over once is what finishes the beginning that was left unfinished.

cells.tense: You feel what is new here, and you file it under being a good listener.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Next time someone shares something you feel, take it in out loud for a beat before you give anything back — let one exchange run both directions.
cells.core:
Wanting is doing its work in you. When people ask what is drawing you, your answer sorts it into listening — the useful kind, or none at all. What is at work is a pull toward light; what is on record is being a good pair of ears. Those are close and not the same, and the people asking can hear the gap.
Try letting an exchange with one person go both ways this week. When something is offered, take it — let it land where it arrived — before offering anything back. You may be surprised how unfamiliar that is, and what it tells you about the pull you have been filing under listening.
cells.sheetLine: The pull is yours, filed under listening.

attempts.check: The draft says the person has stopped feeling what draws them; the record only supports the capacity being open and unused at the threshold, not any claim about what has gone quiet. A reader could reasonably say the lid is still up and they just haven't had a reason to open it yet, not that they've shut it. The ask survives being wrong because noticing what faintly pulls requires nothing of the past and returns something either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying something once broke this open and now it can't be — I have no record of that, and the seated version stays with what the capacity is doing in a moment they could recognize.
